thread:
support_ben: Heads-up — multiple Dedicated customers in eu-south are seeing large spikes in 503/placement-fail errors and visible throttling since ~08:15 UTC. Ticket CI-9482 opened by customer_ops_lucy. Impact: reduced throughput, retries, some timeouts.

sre_jen: On it. Can you paste the customer request IDs / sample logs?

support_ben: Pasting one snippet from the customer's unsuccessful requests: 
```
2026-02-11T08:18:03Z ERROR placement_failure request_id=ac12f2 status=503 reason="no compatible host" pool=dedicated-eu-south
2026-02-11T08:18:04Z WARN scheduling queue_length=184 pending_tokens=12
```
Also they reported a surge of latency before the failures: p95 jumped to 2.6s on their reserved pool.

eng_kyle: Reproduced locally against a staging Dedicated pool with a load script => we see queueing and slow KV cache thrash. Suspect one of the hosts is being noisy (GPU memory pressure + long preemption-retries).

maria_pm: Customer is on a Reserved contract, SLA degraded. They're asking for immediate mitigation and root cause.

autoscaler-bot: Autoscaler event: downscale block triggered at 08:10 UTC for pool dedicated-eu-south due to host health flapping. Attempts to place new allocations are being queued.

sre_jen: Looks like autoscaler blocked because healthcheck failures on three hosts in the pool. Those hosts show GPU OOM and I/O stalls in dmesg. Marking noisy neighbor suspicion.

infra_alex: I'm pulling host metrics now. One node (node-eu-s-17) has sustained 98% GPU util for the last 40m, other nodes getting backpressure. I/O latency for NVMe on that host is high.

support_ben: Customer asked whether this is a billing issue — they're being charged for retries. We need clear communication.

customer_ops_lucy: FYI customer CI-9482 says: "Our app experienced repeated 503s and many client-side retries, effective throughput dropped by ~60% for 30 minutes". They want credit and a timeline.

eng_kyle: Immediate mitigations attempted: 1) cordon node-eu-s-17, 2) reduce default batch size for affected pool, 3) enable fallback routing to eu-west1 for that customer. Cordon worked but placement backlog remains for queued requests.

sre_jen: Quick repro steps I used: 
1) spawn 150 concurrent sessions pinned to that Dedicated pool
2) send steady 30 rps generation requests with seq len 512
3) observe scheduling queue length climb and placement 503s

sre_jen: Logs from scheduler: 
```
2026-02-11T08:22:11Z INFO scheduling try_place request_id=fd33 status=pending pool=dedicated-eu-south
2026-02-11T08:22:14Z ERROR scheduling place_failed request_id=fd33 reason="insufficient_active_hosts"
```

infra_alex: We replaced node-eu-s-17's NVMe on the fly and drained it. After drain, autoscaler allowed new allocations again. But there was a 12m window where placement queue had a >150 backlog.

maria_pm: Any idea why autoscaler didn't provision spare capacity faster? Is the autoscaler policy too conservative?

eng_kyle: Policy has cooldown and capacity buffer set low for cost reasons. We saw slow reaction when multiple hosts flapped. We'll propose temporary policy relaxation for eu-south and an emergency cap-ex for spare pool.

sre_jen: Root cause (working theory): single noisy host with underlying NVMe slowness caused long-running GPU tasks to occupy slot and trigger health flaps; autoscaler cooldown and small buffer caused placement backlog; scheduler returned 503s rather than redirecting.

support_ben: Customer asked for immediate workaround: they accepted temporary failover to eu-west1 for traffic above 90% latency. I enabled routing override for their account.

customer_ops_lucy: Confirmed customer accepted the failover. They want SLA credit and a postmortem.

maria_pm: Action items: 
- infra_alex to document hardware failure and replacement steps (done).
- eng_kyle + sre_jen to propose autoscaler tuning (increase buffer, faster scale-up) and safer fallback logic (prefer model-variant fallback) — due EOD.
- support_ben to coordinate customer communication and credit proposal.
- ops to add a guard that avoids returning 503 for queued placements for X minutes and instead routes to fallback when available.

eng_kyle: Temporary mitigations deployed: decreased autoscaler cooldown from 5m -> 90s (eu-south), increased spare buffer from 1 -> 3, added immediate soft-fallback to region when queue_length > 50. Monitoring dashboards updated.

sre_jen: Post-incident notes: need test harness that simulates noisy GPU host + autoscaler flapping to catch this in CI.

support_ben: Customer notified and offered pro-rated credit for the 30m degradation window. Waiting for approver.

maria_pm: We'll run a short internal blameless postmortem and publish to customers. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
